faqs.q: What are the three main pillars of sustainable development?
faqs.a: The three pillars are economic progress, environmental protection and social wellbeing. Sustainable development tries to balance all three, so that growth today meets present needs without reducing the ability of future generations to meet theirs.

faqs.q: What are some simple examples of sustainable practices in a home or office?
faqs.a: Common examples include saving water, rainwater harvesting, using energy-efficient lights and appliances, separating dry and wet waste, cutting down on unnecessary packaging and reusing materials where possible. Regularly checking water and electricity use also helps spot waste early.

faqs.q: Why is waste segregation important for sustainability?
faqs.a: Separating recyclable and non-recyclable waste at the source makes collection, recycling and safe disposal much easier and cheaper. It reduces the amount of waste sent to landfills and allows more material to be reused, but it works best when households, organisations and local authorities all take part.

faqs.q: How does technology help make cities more sustainable?
faqs.a: Technology such as digital energy management, automated water monitoring, smart transport systems and data-based planning helps identify where resources are being wasted. These tools only deliver results when they are properly maintained, run by trained staff and fed with reliable data.
